name: simutrans
why: An open-source transport simulation game with a deep economy model, a strange old-school corner of simulation that rewards long sessions.

brief.what_it_is: Simutrans is a freeware, open-source transport simulator in which you run a transport company. You build networks by rail, road, ship and air to move passengers, mail and goods between districts, cities, public buildings, industries and tourist attractions. Maps can be any size and need not be square. The game is played with a graphical front end, and it can also run multiplayer with a server that friends join. The homepage does not describe the economy model in detail, so the scout note's 'deep economy model' is unverified.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage pitches it as a way to build 'a transport network you always dreamed of' and to establish a successful transport company. The README gives no further framing.
brief.how_it_works: Each pakset is a separate set of graphics and data (objects, buying prices, maintenance costs, themes) that changes the gameplay, so every pakset is effectively a new game. The game itself is built from C++ source with make, MSVC or CMake, and it needs a Simutrans installation (a pakset) to run. The README says you can start the game with -use_workdir to point it at an existing installation.

brief.install_notes: The homepage offers a download (version 125.0 listed). The README also points to Steam and Linux package managers via pkgs.org. Paksets are needed to run the game and are not bundled with the code; they carry their own license. Building from source needs zlib, bzip2 or zstd, libpng, freetype and, on Linux and macOS, SDL2 (SDL2 is optional but recommended on Windows). Optional libraries include miniupnpc (easy server), fluidsynth or SDL2_mixer (MIDI), and fontconfig. Windows builders use MSVC with vcpkg or MSYS2. setup-mingw.sh and setup-debian.sh scripts fetch libraries on those platforms, and macOS uses Homebrew. The README describes cross-compiling from Linux to Windows as a separate wiki topic. The brew formula's listed executables (makeobj, nettool, simutrans) are not mentioned anywhere I read.
brief.standout: Simutrans is an old-school transport sim with a long history: it began in 1997 under Hansjörg Malthaner, who retired around 2004, and a community team now maintains it. Its most distinctive feature is that paksets are swappable graphics and rules packs, so one engine yields very different games. The Artistic License 1.0 and the translation and painting calls for help also give it an unusually open community feel.
brief.status: maintained. The homepage copyright runs 2016 to 2026 and lists download version 125.0. The README is active, pointing to a live forum, a translator web tool and a wiki, and it describes an ongoing nightly build. I did not see a last-commit date, so the exact recency of commits is unknown.
brief.caveats: Building from source is involved: you pick among three build systems, install many libraries, and in some cases run platform scripts or cross-compile. Paksets are required to play and are separate from the code. The README says most people should use the stable release, not nightly. Contributions go to the forum rather than GitHub pull requests, and the README tells people not to open PRs there. The GitHub repository is a mirror of SVN, and the README states that the SVN repository is the main one. I found the GitHub page by guessing its URL; the homepage does not link to it.
